title: Homogeneity
text:
Live in a neighborhood that is homogeneous.
People belong to a single religion and the vast majority of the residents have a European heritage.
There are a handful of people from other regions of the world.
Namely Asia, Latin America and Africa.

When we first moved into the area, a C family from Taiwan greeted us.
They had 5 children, their last 4 children were the same age as our four.
In addition there was another L family from Taiwan.
One family were musically talented and performed regularly at church.
Afterwards people would congratulate us.
We tried to explain that it was the C family from Taiwan.
After a while we stopped explaining and accepted their appreciation

Years passed and a number of Asian families have come and gone.
Recently a Korean C family joined.
Our identity remain mixed, indistinguishable to many of the neighbors.
A member of the congregation said that he had 2 Korean families mixed.
He often asked me how the overseas trip was when I hadn’t traveled.

Once I said,

I have difficulty distinguishing ward members since they all look alike

The listener recognized the humor and we had a good laugh together.

title: Historian Records
text:
Hanshin the wanderer
Hanshin needed a home. Once found he flourished
However, once his work was done. He was targeted and killed.
Good question 👍 — the Han dynasty (206 BCE – 220 CE) produced, preserved, and canonized many of the foundational Chinese works on warfare, governance, and statecraft. Some were written earlier (in the Warring States or Qin) but became standards and official references during the Han. Here’s a structured overview:

title: Historian Records
text:
⚔️ Warfare & Military Thought

Sunzi Bingfa (孫子兵法, Art of War) – by Sun Tzu (pre-Han, ~5th century BCE)

Became canonical under the Han; generals like Han Xin applied its strategies.
Focus: deception, flexibility, and psychological warfare.

Wu Zi (吳子) – by Wu Qi (Warring States general).

Emphasized discipline, logistics, and civil-military relations.

Wei Liaozi (尉繚子) – a Qin/Han text.

Practical guidance for rulers: military organization, law, agriculture, governance linked to war-making.

Tai Gong’s Six Secret Teachings (太公六韜, Liutao) – attributed to Jiang Ziya (Zhou strategist).

Focus on civil and military balance, leadership, and moral authority in warfare.


👉 These, along with other texts, were later collected into the Seven Military Classics (武經七書) (canonized in the Song dynasty), but the Han dynasty already circulated and studied them.

title: Historian Records
text:
🏛️ Governance, Law, and Statecraft

Book of Documents (尚書, Shangshu)

Ancient collection of speeches and edicts; used in the Han as a Confucian classic for legitimizing rule.

Records of the Grand Historian (史記, Shiji) – by Sima Qian (c. 94 BCE)

Not a manual, but a massive history covering rulers, generals, and statecraft — provided models (good and bad) for governance.

Book of Han (漢書, Hanshu) – by Ban Gu (1st century CE)

Official dynastic history; detailed accounts of institutions, law, economy, and military campaigns.

The Spring and Autumn Annals (春秋, Chunqiu) + Commentaries

Treated as a Confucian manual of rulership and morality.

Huang-Lao Texts (黃老學) – blending Daoism, Legalism, and pragmatism.

Popular especially in the early Han for governance emphasizing minimal interference + strong law.

Statutes and Ordinances of the Second Year (二年律令, Ernian lüling)

Excavated Han legal code, showing actual laws enforced in governance.

title: Historian Records
text:
📌 Takeaway

Military standards: The Han revered earlier classics (Sunzi, Wuzi, Wei Liaozi, Liutao) as guides, with generals like Han Xin embodying their application.
Governance standards: Confucian classics (Shangshu, Chunqiu), historical works (Shiji, Hanshu), and legal codes shaped how emperors and officials ruled.
Together, these became the intellectual backbone of Han statecraft — a mix of Confucian morality, Legalist structure, and strategic pragmatism.

Records of the Grand Historian
https://namu.wiki/w/%EC%82%AC%EA%B8%B0(%EC%97%AD%EC%82%AC%EC%B1%85)
Great question. Sima Qian’s Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji) is not just a chronology—it’s a literary and philosophical work that weaves together history, biography, morality, and political thought. Here are the major themes scholars usually highlight:


1. The Mandate of Heaven & Cyclical History


Dynasties rise and fall because of virtue (de) or the loss of it.

Heaven grants or withdraws legitimacy depending on rulers’ morality and ability.

Shiji illustrates this cycle through narratives of Xia, Shang, Zhou, Qin, and Han.





2. Human Agency vs. Fate


Tension between individual choices and forces beyond control.

Figures like Xiang Yu (the failed conqueror) show the tragedy of brilliance undone by circumstance.

Sima Qian suggests that fate sets limits, but human judgment and character still matter.





3. Morality, Virtue, and Exemplars


History as moral instruction: good rulers uphold ritual, benevolence, and justice; bad rulers indulge in cruelty and excess.

Biographies highlight models (Confucius, ministers of Zhou) and warnings (tyrannical Qin Shi Huang, corrupt officials).





4. The Role of Officials and Advisors


Emphasis on the importance of wise ministers and loyal remonstrators.

Many biographies of courtiers, generals, and strategists stress loyalty, courage, or betrayal.

A warning that rulers who ignore good advice invite ruin.





5. The Ordinary and the Marginalized


Sima Qian breaks ground by including merchants, assassins, wandering knights, astrologers, jesters, etc.

These stories show that history is not only about kings but also about those at society’s edges.





6. Heroism and Tragedy


Admiration for bold individuals who challenge fate, even if they fail.

The tragic arcs of figures like Jing Ke (the would-be assassin of the Qin king) or Qu Yuan (the poet-statesman) highlight human dignity amid defeat.





7. Memory and Legacy


Sima Qian stresses the importance of recording deeds for posterity, even when the person failed in life.

His own preface, written after his disgrace and castration, underscores the theme: history gives people lasting voice beyond shame or death.





8. Integration of Myth, History, and Philosophy


The Shiji blends legendary origins (Yellow Emperor, Yao, Shun) with verifiable historical records.

It is both a Confucian moral history and an effort to preserve cultural memory as a unified narrative.



✅ In sum:

The Shiji is about the rise and fall of power, the tension between virtue and ambition, and the human struggle against fate. It’s simultaneously a political manual, a collection of moral biographies, and a deeply personal meditation on history and memory.

Would you like me to build a visual diagram of these themes (like a thematic map or cluster chart) to pair with the timeline you already have?

  ) +

  ) +

    axis.text.y = element_blank(),

The Records of the Grand Historian (史記 Shǐjì) is one of the most important works in Chinese history and literature. Here’s an overview in plain, interview-style language:



What It Is


Written by Sima Qian (司馬遷), a court historian during the Han Dynasty (around 91 BCE).

It is the first comprehensive history of China, covering more than 2,000 years—from the legendary Yellow Emperor (~2600 BCE) through the reign of Emperor Wu of Han.

Contains 130 chapters, blending history, biography, philosophy, and storytelling.





Structure
The work is divided into five sections:


Basic Annals (本紀 Běnjì) – Chronicles of emperors and ruling houses.

Chronological Tables (年表 Niánbiǎo) – Timelines to keep events across states and dynasties aligned.

Treatises (書 Shū) – Thematic essays on subjects like music, economics, law, astronomy, and rituals.

Hereditary Houses (世家 Shìjiā) – Histories of feudal lords and major noble families.

Biographies (列傳 Lièzhuàn) – Lives of notable figures—officials, generals, scholars, foreign peoples, even assassins and merchants.





Why It Matters


Foundation of Chinese Historiography: Established the model for later dynastic histories (正史 Zhèngshǐ).

Literary Value: Written with vivid, often dramatic storytelling; sometimes reads like a novel.

Balanced Perspective: Sima Qian included both emperors and commoners, victors and rebels—unusual for ancient histories.

Moral Voice: Shows his Confucian values but also independence; Sima Qian himself suffered disgrace and castration yet still completed it, turning personal tragedy into a monumental legacy.





Influence


Considered the “father of Chinese history.”

Influenced later historians such as Ban Gu (Book of Han), and even Chinese prose style in general.

Still read today in China and worldwide for insights into leadership, politics, culture, and human character.



👉 In short: The Records of the Grand Historian is a sweeping, 2,000-year account of China’s past, written with literary flair and historical rigor, setting the standard for all future Chinese history writing.

Here’s a timeline-style summary of the eras covered in the Records of the Grand Historian (Shǐjì):

title: Historian Records
text:
Timeline of the Shiji
(Legendary → Early Dynasties → Han)

Legendary & Mythical Era


Yellow Emperor (Huangdi) ~2600 BCE

Considered the cultural ancestor of the Chinese people.

Yao & Shun ~2300–2100 BCE

Sage-kings, paragons of virtue and good governance.





Xia Dynasty (夏朝)


c. 2070–1600 BCE

Semi-legendary first dynasty, founded by Yu the Great (tamed floods).

Ends with the fall of King Jie, a tyrant.





Shang Dynasty (商朝)


c. 1600–1046 BCE

Known for oracle bones (earliest Chinese writing) and ritual bronzes.

Last ruler King Zhou is overthrown by the Zhou.





Zhou Dynasty (周朝)


c. 1046–256 BCE

Western Zhou (1046–771 BCE): Strong central kingship, “Mandate of Heaven” concept.

Eastern Zhou (770–256 BCE): Divides into two eras:


Spring and Autumn (770–476 BCE): Rise of regional lords; Confucius lives.

Warring States (475–221 BCE): Intense rivalry among 7 major states (Qin, Chu, Zhao, Wei, Han, Qi, Yan).







Qin Dynasty (秦朝)


221–206 BCE

Founded by Qin Shi Huang, China’s first emperor.

Unified weights, measures, currency, writing; began Great Wall.

Harsh Legalist rule; collapsed quickly after the emperor’s death.





Han Dynasty (Early/Western Han) (漢朝)


206 BCE – 220 CE (but Shiji stops at Emperor Wu, r. 141–87 BCE).

Founder: Liu Bang (Emperor Gaozu).

Peak: Emperor Wu (Han Wudi) expanded territory, promoted Confucianism, opened trade routes (Silk Road beginnings).

Sima Qian served as court historian during this dynasty.

title: Historian Records
text:
Key Point
The Shiji traces Chinese history from myth to Han, about 2,000 years of rulers, wars, reforms, and culture.

It sets a framework: sage beginnings → dynastic rise and fall → unification under Qin → flourishing Han.

title: Welcome Home Elder
text:
Work for a small company in a small town, around 300 and 100,000 persons respectively.
Surprised to hear from 3 colleagues that their daughters and a nephew were called to labor in Korea, all entering the MTC on the same day.
The probability of this occurrence would be close to winning a lottery.
Like sending the space force cadets on a long-term mission, from a single neighborhood.
Often, I would check with their fathers and uncle to learn about their experiences and where they were serving.
성남, 서산, 강남, 군산, 청주, 천안.
Sisters got to serve in the Wards where we had relatives.
And when Sister K visited that relative, she was able to deliver a package from home.

18 months and 24 months away from the comforts of a home is a sacrifice.
In some sense, this is an adventure, a spiritual one.
Many are visiting and sampling countries and cultures around the globe.

How much time is necessary time to be immersed in a culture and understand its influence on people?

It is not days or weeks but months or years, based on my experience.
A consistent exposure to culture and an increased understanding of the language helps.
Always taken back by the language comprehension and command of nuance and subtlety of 사투리 (dialect) by those returning from the Korean Language Missions.
Even more amazing is when they express that it was the best times of their lives.

Sisters had returned home earlier this year.
Checked back with the colleague,

When is your nephew coming home? He just came home last Thursday.

Let’s have a lunch together.

His brother and a cousin joined as well.
And the father of one of the sisters came as well.
When I saw him, I was surprised how young he looked. Like a high school student.
In fact, I thought his brother was the returned missionary. (His brother is 22, he served in Mexico City area)
I drove with him to test his language skills. No hesitations, he answered all my prompts and asked appropriate questions, all with a zeal of a young man.
Refreshing to be around young people. For that hour, I forgot where I was, what I was eating and what my concerns were. I was taken back to my home, among the people Elder B served.
He mentioned the need for older missionaries. And how wonderful they are.
Made me reflect on Psalm 8:2

Through the praise of children and infants you have established a stronghold against your enemies, to silence the foe and the avenger


New International Version

He described his return flight home. There were 40 other missionaries going home.
Instead of flying them separately, the church decided to use the direct flight, ICN to SLC.
Then those missionaries would fly to their eventual destinations.
I imagined them spontaneously breaking into a half dozen song medley in the plane.

Come, Thou Fount of Every Blessing
Be Still, My Soul
Come, Follow Me
A Child’s Prayer
Called to Serve
Savior, Redeemer of My Soul

And the rest of the passengers joining in and singing the 3rd verse.

O’errule mine acts to serve thine ends. Change frowning foes to smiling friends. Chasten my soul till I shall be In perfect harmony with thee.

O gracious God of Israel
Thank you for the lives of these young people and safely bringing them home.

title: Araki San
text:
私は、荒木　実（アラキ　ミノル）といいます。 荒木　誠（アラキ　マコト）の長男です。 Donald（ダンノ）の従兄弟（いとこ　first cousin） になります。 丁寧なお手紙をいただき、ありがとうございます。 とつぜんのことで驚きましたが、とても嬉しかったです。 ダンノや伯母（カチ）のことは、ずっと気になっていました。 父（誠）が、２０１１年に亡くなった後は、連絡できずに 時が過ぎてしまいました。 伯母（カチ）が亡くなったことは、2年ぐらい前に 義理の伯父（Ｒeedさん）のことをWEBで見てた時に知りました。 そして、ダンノの活躍の様子も、少しですが知ることができて、 嬉しかったです。 父が亡くなってからは、親戚との付き合いも殆どなくなり、 詳しくは、あまりわからないのですが、できる限り調べてみます。
ダンノが1970年ごろに日本に来たときの写真を添付してみました。 古い写真なのでかなりぼやけてます。 伯母の両隣が、父（誠）と叔母（ナホ）です。 ダンノと一緒に写っているのが私と姉の由紀子です。
また、連絡させていただきます。 アメリカに帰られたら、ダンノと奥様に宜しくお伝えください。
荒木　実

저는 아라키 미노루(荒木 実)라고 합니다.

아라키 마코토(荒木 誠)의 장남입니다.

도날드(단노)의 사촌 형제(첫 사촌)입니다.
정성 어린 편지 잘 받았습니다.

갑작스러운 연락에 놀랐지만, 매우 기뻤습니다.

단노와 고모(카치) 이야기는 늘 마음에 두고 있었습니다.

아버지(마코토)가 2011년에 돌아가신 후로는 연락하지 못했고

시간만 흘러갔습니다.
고모(카치)가 돌아가셨다는 것은 약 2년 전에

시아버지(리드 씨)에 대해 웹에서 볼 때 알게 되었습니다.

그리고 단노가 활약하는 모습도 조금 알게 되어 기뻤습니다.
아버지가 돌아가신 이후로는 친척들과 거의 연락이 끊겨

자세한 사정은 잘 모르지만, 가능한 한 조사해 보겠습니다.
단노가 1970년경 일본에 왔을 때 찍은 사진을 첨부했습니다.

오래된 사진이라 꽤 흐릿합니다.

고모 양옆에 있는 사람이 아버지(마코토)와 이모(나호)입니다.

단노와 함께 찍힌 사람이 저와 누나 유키코입니다.
또 연락드리겠습니다.

미국에 돌아가시면 단노와 부인께 안부 전해 주세요.
아라키 미노루 드림

My name is Minoru Araki.

I am the eldest son of Makoto Araki.

I am Donald’s first cousin.
Thank you very much for your kind letter.

I was surprised by the sudden contact, but I was very happy.

I have always been concerned about Danno and my aunt Kachi.

After my father (Makoto) passed away in 2011, I was unable to get in touch,

and time just passed by.
I learned that Aunt Kachi passed away about two years ago

when I was looking up information about my uncle-in-law Reed on the web.

I was also happy to learn a little about Danno’s activities.
Since my father passed away, I have had very little contact with relatives,

so I don’t know the details very well, but I will try to find out as much as I can.
I attached a photo from around 1970 when Danno came to Japan.

It is an old photo, so it is quite blurry.

On both sides of my aunt are my father (Makoto) and my aunt (Naho).

In the photo with Danno are my sister Yukiko and me.
I will contact you again.

When you return to America, please give my best regards to Danno and his wife.
Minoru Araki

title: Aging Signs
text:
Few signs that you are aging or aged.
Tears come freely without warning.
Often in private but more and more in public settings.
In times of gladness but more often due to frailties of life.
A recognition that you have more in common with people.
Both familiar and less familiar.
Listen to opinions of others but seldom swayed.
The models that served you well are hard to part with.
A discussion leader said,

Not a testimony of the model, rather the reality behind it.

Less effort to cling to the familiar.
Almost anything can be construed to be nostalgia.
Any number of triggers can remind of a time, place or a person.
Especially times and places that remind us that this life is temporary.
Wishing for persons to be unchanging and eternal, free from constraints of this life.

Try a new channel on Spotify?
Unlikely.
Past is comfortable, unchanging, controllable
Future isn’t

title: Center of Learning
text:
Kyoto (京都) has its temples and shrines.
Suzhou (蘇州 or 苏州) has canals and gardens.
An Dong (안동시/安東市) has its share of 한옥1 and 서원
경주 and 셔울 has administrative and cultural palaces, and religious temples.
However, 안동 has preserved 서원
Similar to temples and shrines, 서원s are usually built on a hill over looking cities or bodies of like rivers, built with a series of building and gates.
These buildings of learning and housing are configured, connected, and positioned to resemble one’s journey in life.
A series of experiences or trials followed by an entry into a higher level of understanding. Symbolically represented by series of gates and a rise in elevation.
서원 layout link
Classical Gardens of Suzhou represents nature or order of universe and symbolically captures universal elements of life taught through Confucianism, Taoism, and Buddhism2.
拙政園 Humble Administrator’s Garden link
서원, the place of learning set in nature, captures elements and intents of temples, shrines, and gardens.
Educating and elevating human souls to a higher levels of understanding.
Nature both teaches and confirms learning and attainment.
By visiting these places, one can assess the understanding of men and his place in the society and the universe.
Although our daily struggles and growth may be small but it is a significant step towards a destined place.
Passing through men or god instituted tests and trials and receiving due attainment.

Appendix A: An Overview of Classical Gardens
Key Features of Suzhou Gardens Small-scale but highly artistic design
Unlike imperial gardens (e.g., in Beijing), Suzhou gardens are private and intimate, designed for reflection and scholarly life.
Principles of design
“Borrowed scenery” (借景): Use of background elements outside the garden.
Balance of elements: Rocks (symbolizing mountains), water (lakes or ponds), plants, and architecture.
Architecture and space
Pavilions, bridges, zigzag corridors, moon gates, lattice windows.
Designed for framing views, seasonal change, and poetic composition.
Symbolism
Every element often holds cultural or philosophical meaning, especially from Confucianism, Taoism, and Buddhism.

section: Appendix B: AI Explanation of 한옥
text:
Appendix B: AI Explanation of 한옥
한옥(韓屋)은 한국의 전통적인 건축 양식으로 지어진 집을 의미합니다. 주로 나무, 흙, 돌, 짚 등을 사용하여 지어지며, 온돌, 대청마루 등 특징적인 구조를 가지고 있습니다. 넓은 의미로는 초가집, 너와집 등 모든 전통 가옥을 포함하지만, 일반적으로는 기와집 형태의 한옥을 떠올리는 경우가 많습니다. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
한옥의 특징:
• 온돌: 구들을 이용해 바닥 난방을 하는 한국 고유의 난방 방식입니다. [7, 7, 8, 8]
• 대청마루: 거실과 같이 넓은 공간으로, 여름철 시원하게 지낼 수 있는 공간입니다. [7, 7, 9, 9, 10, 11, 12]
• 처마: 지붕의 끝 부분이 건물 밖으로 길게 뻗어 나와 여름철 햇볕을 가려주고 겨울철에는 눈과 비를 막아줍니다. [7, 7, 13, 13]
• 자연과의 조화: 풍수지리 사상에 따라 자연 환경과 조화를 이루도록 지어지며, 뒤로는 산을 등지고 앞으로는 물을 바라보는 방향으로 짓는 것이 일반적입니다. [1, 1, 14, 14]
한옥의 종류:
• 초가집: 짚으로 지붕을 이은 집입니다. • 너와집: 나무 판자를 엮어 지붕을 이은 집입니다. • 기와집: 기와로 지붕을 이은 집입니다. [5, 5, 7, 7]
한옥의 장점:
• 친환경적인 건축 재료: 나무, 흙, 돌 등 자연 재료를 사용하여 건강하고 쾌적한 주거 환경을 제공합니다. [2, 2, 5, 5]
• 온돌 난방 시스템: 겨울철 따뜻하고 편안한 난방을 제공합니다. [2, 2, 8, 8, 15]
• 자연과의 조화: 주변 환경과 잘 어울리고 자연의 변화를 느낄 수 있습니다. [1, 1, 14, 14, 16, 17, 18]
• 독특한 아름다움: 전통적인 선과 구조에서 나오는 아름다움을 가지고 있습니다. [13, 13, 19, 19]
최근 한옥의 변화: 최근에는 현대적인 생활 방식에 맞춰 한옥을 개량하거나 새로운 한옥을 짓는 시도가 이루어지고 있습니다. 전통적인 요소를 유지하면서 편리성을 높이고, 현대적인 디자인을 가미하여 새로운 형태의 한옥이 등장하고 있습니다. [20, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25]
AI responses may include mistakes.

title: Return Trip to Bountiful
text:
손자(孫子):
Hi Grandpa, came across some digital photos from the year of the Snake (乙巳)1.
Wasn’t this the period when you were slowing down and transitioning from company funded trips?
The photos told a different story.
Older Me:
That was the year the oldest of your maternal uncles got married, Uncle JH.
Yes, that was post company sponsored travel days. And I thought of taking things slower but your grandma had other ideas.
She was invited to the wedding in Korea and scheduled to travel there.
But I wasn’t – initially.
Like many things in life, women’s willpower changes the outcome.
Soon, I was making travel plans and thinking of people and places to meet and visit.
손자(孫子):
So how did you go about detailed planning? Without specifics of business trips.
Older Me:
We have visited Korea a number of times, but this was the first time only 2 of us traveled.
At that time we had sold the business that required the attention of grandma. Because I was working at the time, chose a 10-day visit duration. Planned around the wedding.
That opened up many options and possibilities.
In addition, a direct flight to Incheon, Korea, had begun just few weeks prior to the visit.2
I had a number of aunts and uncle that were in their 80s and 90s.
My mother’s younger siblings in Korea were, 90 and 87.
My father’s youngest brother was 82.
My mother’s church friend was 90.
Visiting them was my priority.
Plus I wanted to visit my hometown 인천(仁川).
The remaining time would be spent either shopping or visiting sites around the country.
I didn’t know how we could do all of this in 10 days.
We decided to visit 서울성전 at the beginning and at the end of our visit.
And met with the uncle and aunts, the first 4 days we were in Korea.
손자(孫子):
I do remember stories about your aunts and uncles.
I am glad you kept in touch with them over the years.
How did you get in touch with Grandma’s friends, after she had passed away?
Older Me:
We formed a group, LLJK, (이이정강).
We first met in 인천, during the early days of the Church in the area.
We had maintained our friendship with the help of the group chat.
All but L1 had moved to the States, when I told L2 and J that I would be traveling to Korea, they suggested I get in touch with L1, who lived in 마포 area of 서울
L2 warned me that there aren’t many people that would remember me and advised me to visit and enjoy the local food.
L1 met me on a day that was 90+ degrees Farenheit and same amount of humidity.
I wanted to meet my aunt first and then tour the town.
I wondered why he kept avoiding a lunchtime rendenvous
As a compromise, we met at 9AM at 동인천역(東仁川駅)
By 10AM the weather was brutal, I was struggling with the heat and the hilly streets
As we walked, L1 rehearsed the history and people associated with the church in Incheon (인천)
Started in 중앙동, in a rented, converted 2-story building. Recall, one of the floor had a tatami (畳) floor.
Then a government property3 in 답동 was purchased and the existing building was renovated for church use.
Subsequently a new building was built on site. Eventually, all of the 인천 area wards were combined into a single meeting house in 주안.
손자(孫子):
Quite a day. You were lucky that L2 was available and willing to take you to places. How did it feel to walk around the places of birth and growth?
Older Me:
Things had changed dramatically in last 50 years. Except for few places that hadn’t changed, it was like many other places in modern Korea. Vertical growth and no green areas. Almost a feeling of visiting a foreign country.
Except, the memories of people and experiences. Meetings and activities in the old chapel.
Friends that still remember who I was and accept me as who I have become.
손자(孫子):
So did you visit your old church on Sunday?
Older Me:
Yes, I visited 인천1와드. That Ward was composed of the former, 답동, 송도, 주안 Wards
As we were driving towards the new building, I related the conversion story of my mother.
She had studied with the missionaries for nearly 2 years. But she still had some questions. She wrote them down.
When Harold B. Lee visited Korea and my mother attended the fireside All of mother’s questions were answered by the visiting general authority. Mom’s mind was set to join the church - intellectually
Then one afternoon, she dreamed a dream.
In the dream, there were 2 books. She could tell they were the Bible and the Book of Mormon. And a hand appeared and pointing to 2 books and touching them one by one said
She was ready to be baptized.
손자(孫子):
Thanks for sharing that. So did anyone recognize you?
Older Me:
L2 was correct, in a congregation of nearly 150 people only 3 people knew me. L2’s mother. L1’s sister and her husband.
I wondered if this will be similar to how we will be welcomed into the next life. There will be we may know and recognize but only a few would personally escort us through.
That person this time was L2’s mom.
She recounted how she and my mother served in the Stake Primary Presidency, without really understandint the calling.
Then she recounted my mother’s dream about the hand and 2 books. Almost word for word.
My testimony was strengthened. I had come home to my and my family’s Bountiful.
Thank you members of the 인천 area. In particular, thank you Sister 임윤님, Brother 유관종, Sister 이강주. For remembering me, welcoming me, and confirming the faith of my parents.

title: 歸田園居
text:
Recent visit to a large, modern, metropolitan area confirmed a theory.
A suspicion that has been building and partially tested over the years.
I have become a country mouse than a city mouse.
All of the modern conveniences were present.
Clean, well organized streets with buses and subways that served virtually all parts of the city.
Law abiding citizens, adding to the sense of well being and safety.
Modern office and apartment buildings that housed hundreds if not thousand persons in a single edifice.
Places that will satisfy basics as well as un-stated needs in an instant.
In fact, the only thing missing were more customers that will consume all of the material goods that were readily available in this metropolitan area and beyond.
There were few things that I needed coaching up to become more like the citizen of this city.
Like navigating the maze of the underground transportation system. Calling taxis using the new peer to peer network. Ordering food through installed kiosks at each table.
In time, I would become more proficient and could mimic being a local person.
However, there was one trend that proved to be difficult to overlook.
Tasks in big city were mostly transactional.
No room, or more accurately no time for getting personal or have a human interaction.
In an area, covered with as if 人山人海, I felt alone. Tides of people in the morning and even more people in the evening hours.
I would not know how to adjust to this setting where people appear to congregate and get things done, then retire to their areas of refuge, into their cubicles in the sky.
I could adjust, but given a choice, I will take a small town with its inconveniences over a big town living.
談的談 說的說
小城故事真不錯
請你的朋友一起來
小城來做客
Talking here, and chatting there,
Small town stories are so fine.
Bring your friends along with you,
Come and spend some time.

title: A 2 Minute Drama
text:
Abraham Lincoln’s Gettysburg Address has 272 words.
It can be delivered in 2 or 3 minutes, depending on the speaker.
It is considered one of the most powerful speeches in American history, known for its clarity, moral conviction and rhetorical impact, according to AI summary.
Despite its brevity and maybe because of it, the meaning and purpose and our role in democracy is forcefully taught and remembered.
Perhaps these songs are about our temporal home
With reference to our eternal home.
While cleaning out some drawers, found a set of cassettes that I have owned since the 1980s.
ChatGPT further highights key charactistics.
The unique feeling of deep sorrow and unresolved grief. Nearly all Koreans can relate to this, especially if they are baby boomers.
Perhaps that is the reason, Korean Dramas are infused with longing, nature, love and nostalgia, along with ever unresolved feeling of 한(恨)
Each cassette covers 60 minutes of emotional, polar spectrum of emotions.
Take a trip among 비목(碑木) and ride among clouds.
Think of departed ones as one witnesses sunset among barley fields.
Think of Tang Dynasty poet, 薛濤 (설도) work, 춘망사(春望詞)
Adapted into a lyrical song called 동심초 (同心草)

After hearing the songs and understanding lyrics from yesteryears, the lonliness is lessened.
Understand dreams and aspirations of the older generation.
Better understand my own short comings.
That translates into a renewed resolve.

title: A 2 Minute Drama
text:
Key Characteristics of 한국가곡:
Lyrics in Korean
Unlike Western lieder (like Schubert or Schumann), Korean art songs are sung in standard Korean, often using poetry by modern Korean poets or texts that evoke traditional Korean values and imagery.
Western Musical Form
The structure, harmony, and vocal techniques are borrowed from Western classical music, particularly the German lied and French mélodie traditions.
Emphasis on Emotion (정서, jeong-seo)
Themes often revolve around longing, nature, love, nostalgia, and han (한) — the uniquely Korean feeling of deep sorrow or unresolved grief.
Piano Accompaniment
Most Korean art songs are composed for a solo voice with piano, similar to Western art songs.
Performance Tradition

These songs are frequently performed in recitals, competitions, and school curriculums for vocal students in Korea.

title: Convenience and Comfort
text:
Visited a place where food was fit for Goldilocks.
It wasn’t too spicy, too salty, but just right.
Took many photos, some came out better than I expected.
In fact, all of them were technically just right, as algorithm dictated it to be.
Didn’t have to make any travel plans.
Hosts took care of it, I just had to be ready and they chauffeured me from places to places using the latest navigation tools.

During the visit, I didn’t get lost – while we were with locals.
Consequently, I never learned how to figure out directions or where I was visiting.
By looking at metadata on photos, I could retrace places I visited.
In the days past, I would be asking directions even after planning with physical maps.
Looking for landmarks, such as banks or natural indicators that provides directional anchors.
Also studying the sun’s position aided in determining the direction in the absence of landmarks such as mountains.
This approach was mistake-prone but after a day or so, one usually figured out the lay of the land.






Figure 1: 창덕궁, near 37°34’45.4”N 126°59’32.4”E




One rainy afternoon, I ventured out on my own.
Initial thinking was that I could locate palaces, since most landmarks remained same in that part of town.
I miscalculated.
My assistant was the locally made, on-line map, which had details often lacking multi-purpose maps made outside the country.
However, since I couldn’t figure out my current location, the e-Maps were not as helpful.
To figure out the immediate location, I had to move about, which was difficult to notice on a small phone screen.
Finally resorted to asking people where I needed to go.
Some were friendly and some were helpful, some were neither.
At last, tried the strategy of following tourists to the tourist destination.






Figure 2: Within 비원



Food was not only presented well and flavored ideally, but also there were over abundance of it.
Growing up, food was scarce and meals were served plain.
We mostly ate vegetables, fishes and occasional meat-enhanced soups.
Food was local and seldom got to taste cuisine from other locations
We tasted meat, a couple times a year, usually during holidays or birthdays of older people.
On this trip, we got to sample food from all regions of the country, while in the capital city.
Special occasion food was available on-demand, all hours of the day.
One could eat food from days gone by as well as order food that was from other countries.
At a wedding banquet, the buffet line featured 5 separate offerings.
A line of traditional Korean food, followed by seafood selection, fruit and salad, and dessert.
An hour and half allotted time was not enough to sample all the food and to visit with relatives.^[in the wedding venues, scheduled are tightly set and each couple has 30 to 40 minutes to use the main hall and guests are directed to the dining hall afterwards, before the next couple starts their cycle of activities]
Chose to visit with relatives, for some it was nearly 30 years since we last saw them.






Figure 3: Closer to Food from earlier years



The society had transformed from scarcity and inconvenient mode to one of utmost abundance and comfort.
During 50 years, the pace of growth and transformation has been remarkable.
Kudos to the people of Korea their achievements that borders on miracle.
As an observer of the change, it seemed that in days of past, one was faced with daily challenges and inconvenience.
Lack of food and walk to nearly all places.
In the present day, there are more food than the population 2 or 3 times can consume.
In addition, one has to look for ways to exercise, to find a way to walk to places and and try to get lost and try the personal navigation skills rather than rely on electronic help.

Not to suggest that those days were preferable to present day.
Days of poverty, hunger and physical demands

title: Guides and Limits

Main role of fathers is to set limits and to show how to live within that boundary or constraint.

My mother was the oldest, she had a sister that remained in North, due to bombings she was not able to join the family. There were daughter and son that perished. So mother and the 5th child is significant. There were 2 other sisters and an uncle.
Both families survived physically without fathers.
Emotionally there were scars from lingering, slow-defeating habits
Smoking tobacco and drinking alcohol.
These are entry drugs.
Leads to gambling and eventually abandonment and destroyer of home.
My father put an end to it, he was iconolast.
Can one over come? Yes but much easier with father present.

The Korean War Veterans Memorial in Washington, D.C., honors those who served in the Korean War (1950–1953).

title: Remembrance of Participants
text:
Timeline

1986 – Authorization: U.S. Congress passes Public Law 99-572 authorizing the memorial.
1989 – Design Selection: A nationwide competition selects a team led by architect Frank Gaylord (sculptor) and Cooper-Lecky Architects.
1993 – Construction Begins: Groundbreaking ceremony held on June 14, 1993 (Flag Day).
1995 – Dedication: Dedicated on July 27, 1995, the 42nd anniversary of the Korean Armistice Agreement. President Bill Clinton and South Korean President Kim Young-sam attended.
2016 – Wall of Remembrance Legislation: Congress approves an addition to honor fallen service members by name.
2021–2022 – Wall of Remembrance Construction: Built and officially dedicated on July 27, 2022.

title: Remembrance of Participants
text:
Symbolism in the Memorial

Nineteen Soldier Statues

Represent the U.S. Army, Navy, Air Force, and Marine Corps.
Ethnically diverse to reflect the makeup of American forces.
Moving in formation through a field of juniper bushes and granite strips meant to symbolize Korea’s rugged terrain.

Reflections = 38 Soldiers

Statues reflected in the polished granite Mural Wall double the number to 38 — symbolic of the 38th parallel, the dividing line between North and South Korea.

Mural Wall

Over 2,400 sandblasted photographic images from the Korean War, taken from National Archives and the military branches, representing all services and support roles.

Pool of Remembrance

Surrounded by inscriptions:

“Freedom Is Not Free”
Casualty figures: 36,574 Americans dead, 103,284 wounded, 7,200+ KATUSA killed.


Wall of Remembrance (2022)

Lists names of 36,634 Americans and 7,174 KATUSA troops who died.
Brings the memorial in line with the Vietnam and WWII memorials, which also list names.

title: Take Images

Used to be phone-based cameras tried to catch up to DSLR (Digital Single Lens Reflex) cameras.

Apple – iPhone “Shot on iPhone” Campaign (2015–present)
Apple heavily pushed the idea that iPhone photos could rival professional cameras.
Billboards, commercials, and online ads showcased real photos taken by iPhone users, sometimes directly compared to DSLR-like quality.
With the iPhone 7 Plus (2016) and its Portrait Mode, Apple began directly suggesting it could replace DSLR portrait photography.
If the metrics are the number of flawless images taken and shared.
Then we have a clear winner – cellphone cameras have won.
However, if one measures the progress towards understanding, pursuing and capturing, drawing with light.
Then the game isn’t over.
The word photography comes from Greek roots:
“phōs / phōtós” (φῶς / φωτός) → light
“graphé / graphein” (γραφή / γράφειν) → drawing, writing

So literally, photography means “drawing with light.”


Is it possible to make progress without making mistakes?
Recently erased 110 GBytes of images on the phone.
Taken over 14 months, there were over 20000 images
Roughly averaged 50 images per day.
I could save just the “highlights”
Take the picture you want to draw, rather than hand the control over to camera brain.

“My (DSLR/Mirrorless) camera images are just as good.

title: Reed J Irvine
text:
IRVINE, Reed (John) 1922-2004
OBITUARY NOTICE— See index for CA sketch: Born September 29, 1922, in Salt Lake City, UT; died of complications following a stroke November 16, 2004, in Rockville, MD. Consumer advocate, economist, and author. Irvine was the founder of the watchdog group Accuracy in Media (AIM). A graduate of the University of Utah, where he earned a B.A. in 1942, Irvine acted as an intelligence officer in the Pacific theater during World War II. After the war, he returned to school, first at the University of Washington and then attending Oxford University on a Fulbright scholarship. He graduated from Oxford in 1951 and was hired as an economist at the Federal Reserve System board of governors. From 1963 until 1977 he was international finance adviser for the Far East section. It was while working for the Federal Reserve that he got his idea to form AIM out of frustration with what he considered to be the slanted liberal perspective of the media. Founded in 1969, AIM often worked to get equal air time on television and space in newspapers for its more conservative views, and Irvine also wrote a syndicated column that was printed in about one hundred newspapers. The organization saw its most influential period during the years Ronald Reagan was president, declining somewhat in the 1990s as Irvine became increasingly preoccupied with investigating conspiracy theories, such as his belief that the crash of TWA Flight 800 was caused by a missile and that White House deputy counsel Vincent W. Foster Jr. might have actually been murdered, not a victim of suicide, in 1993. In 1985, Irvine started a venture similar to AIM, known as Accuracy in Academia, but its conservative agenda and desire to wield influence over academic freedoms found fewer sympathizers. Irvine remained chair of AIM until 2003, when he retired as chairman emeritus. He was the author of Media Mischief and Misdeeds (1984).

from Encyclopedia.com, https://www.encyclopedia.com/arts/educational-magazines/irvine-reed-john-1922-2004


Accuracy in Academia (AIA)’s founder, Reed Irvine, died November 16, 2004 at the age of 82. Born in 1922, he served his country in World War II as a marine. He really never stopped serving his country.
He started Accuracy in Media (AIM), AIA’s parent organization, in 1969, to scrutinize the then-dominant old media at a time when few questioned its reporting. From the time he retired as a Federal Reserve Board economist in the 1970s until late last year, when he suffered a serious heart attack, he worked for AIM full-time.
It is fair to say that the so-called new media—Fox News, talk radio and even internet blogs—that prove the reporting of the venerable CBS News and company to be inaccurate are rushing through a door that Reed Irvine opened when he started going head-to-head with media heavyweights such as then-Washington Post editor Ben Bradlee.
Reed Irvine started AIA in 1985 because he saw that too many professors were using classrooms the way that too many reporters used newsrooms—to influence events rather than provide actual accounts of the past and present. He served as chairman of AIA until his death.
Since the 1980s, his standards have guided AIA. In his late seventies, he went toe to toe with demonstrators who attempted to disrupt an AIA conference at Columbia University in New York City.
When I first came to AIA last year, I read an e-mail that Reed forwarded around the office. He answered one of AIM’s critics by writing, “Show me one thing that we have written that is inaccurate.” No one could.
On October 22, 1985, Izvestiya, the state-run newspaper in the then-still existent Soviet Union, ran an article on the founding of Accuracy in Academia (AIA). Of all of the press coverage that AIA has received in its history, the Izvestiya write-up is arguably the most historically significant. Entitled ‘The Hunt For Freethinkers,’ the piece took aim at the then-infant group’s purpose.
“By the look of things, henceforth students, with the start of their activities, will take out fountain pens and tape recorders,” Izvestiya predicted. “Teachers at universities are quivering with fear,” the Soviet press organ reported. “They tremble at the utterance of each word.”
“For who knows?,” Izvestiya asked rhetorically. “Are the students taking notes on their lectures for their own purposes, or are they listening for the purpose of reporting what the teacher says to the ultra-right organization, Accuracy in Academia?”
Izvestiya normally confined itself to attacking U. S. government policies and American society in general. Leveling a front-page broadside at a small non-profit group represented somewhat of an editorial departure for the journal. The attention Izvestiya devoted to AIA, then, gave the watchdog group quite a distinction.
“The reactionary newspaper, The Washington Times, crows over the report that Accuracy in Academia, which has only existed for a few days, already has gathered voluntary informants on 110 university campuses throughout the United States,” Izvestiya noted.
“At the call of their spiritual mentor, worshippers and apprentices of McCarthy hunt for teachers who have the courage to adhere to liberal convictions,” according to Izvestiya. The McCarthy that Izvestiya refers to is the late Sen. Joseph R. McCarthy, R-WI, famous for his investigations of communists in U. S. government jobs.
“By such measures, these teachers are labeled ‘Marxists,’ which in contemporary America is pregnant with the most serious consequences,” Izvestiya asserted. “For example, political science professor Bertell Ollman knows this from personal experience for he dared admit that he was actually on the side of Marxism. Solely because of that he was not allowed to compete to fill a position at the University of Maryland.”
Six years after the Izvestiya article appeared, the Soviet Union itself imploded and the Cold War ended. This year, AIA celebrates 19 years of life and is still in business. Izvestiya is still in business too, although under new management. And by the way, so is Bertell Ollman. A professor of politics at New York University, he teaches ‘Socialist Theory’ for undergraduates and ‘Communism’ and ‘Methods of Political and Social Analysis’ at the graduate level.
Because professors such as Ollman, and their understudies, are still in business, teaching the history of the Cold War from the Evil Empire’s perspective, AIA continues its work, as our founder would have wanted us to.
Accuracy in Academia founder, Reed Irvine,
died November 16, 2004 at the age of 82.
His legacy as a true advocate of democracy lives on.
Reed Irvine, R. I. P.
by: Malcolm A. Kline, November 17, 2004

title: Absolute Self-Effacement
text:
Humility is just as much the opposite of self-abasement as it is of self-exaltation.
To be humble is not to make comparisons.
Secure in its reality, the self is neither better nor worse, bigger nor smaller, than anything else in the universe.
It is–is nothing, yet at the same time one with everything.
It is in this sense that humility is absolute self-effacement.

To be nothing in the self-effacement of humility, yet, for the sake of the task, to embody its whole weight and importance in your earing, as the one who has been called to undertake it.
To give to people, works, poetry, art, what the self can contribute, and to take, simply and freely, what belongs to it by reason of its identity.
Praise and blame, the winds of success and adversity, blow over such a life without leaving a trace or upsetting its balance.”
― Dag Hammarskjöld, Markings

title: Mahler’s 2nd Symphony
text:
AI Summary
Gustav Mahler’s Symphony No. 2 in C minor (“Resurrection”) (premiered 1895) is over a century old, yet it continues to resonate with audiences and performers worldwide. Its relevance today comes from a mix of musical innovation, emotional depth, and timeless themes.

title: Mahler’s 2nd Symphony
text:
Why Mahler’s 2nd Still Matters Today

1. Universal Themes

The symphony wrestles with life, death, despair, hope, and transcendence.
Mahler takes the listener from funeral rites (first movement) through struggles, irony, and grief, to an overwhelming vision of renewal and resurrection.
These are existential questions that remain as urgent in the 21st century as they were in Mahler’s time.



2. Scale and Power

One of the first truly monumental symphonies: massive orchestra, organ, vocal soloists, and chorus.
Modern audiences still find the sheer sonic impact overwhelming — it fills concert halls in ways few works can.
The finale’s choral eruption of “Aufersteh’n, ja aufersteh’n wirst du” (“You will rise again”) is often described as a life-changing moment in live performance.



3. Bridge Between Eras

Combines Romantic tradition (Beethoven, Brahms) with innovations pointing toward 20th-century modernism.
Its use of folk-like melodies, irony, collage of styles, and spiritual searching prefigures Shostakovich, Stravinsky, and even film music.



4. Resonance with Crisis and Renewal

After wars, pandemics, and social upheavals, audiences connect with its narrative of struggle → collapse → renewal.
It’s often programmed in times of mourning or remembrance (e.g., after 9/11, orchestras turned to it for healing).



5. Personal Connection

Mahler wrote the work while grappling with mortality and meaning. His deeply personal struggle gives the symphony an authentic voice that transcends its era.
Today, listeners facing their own uncertainties hear their emotions mirrored in the music.

title: Mahler’s 2nd Symphony
text:
In short
Mahler’s Resurrection Symphony endures because it is more than music — it’s an experience of grief, hope, and transcendence. Its emotional honesty, monumental sound, and universal questions keep it fresh, urgent, and profoundly moving for modern audiences.
